summary: Hans T. Bakker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink (c. 1970–1982). He held posts at Utrecht University (c. 1985–1996) and the University of Groningen (c. 1996–2013).
Hans Urs von Balthasar was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Zurich from around 1923 to 1928 and under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (c. 1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (c. 1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit was a religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and doctoral supervisor Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded as Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indology scholar who studied under Eduard Hermann and doctoral supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt.

Hanung Kim is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Har Bilas Sarda was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta from around 1884 to 1888 and served as a judge at the Court of Small Causes, Ajmer (c. 1923–1924).
Har Dayal was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Delhi and at SOAS University of London from around 1927 to 1932.
Har Dutt Sharma was an Indology scholar who served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and held a post at Hindu College, Delhi (attested 1957).

Hara Prasad Sastri was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).
Harabhatta Sastri is an Indology scholar who served in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, where his post is attested in 1918 (as pandit), 1922, and 1945.
Harabhatha Shastri is an Indology scholar who held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911 and in 1916 as a Pandit.

Harald Hauptmann was a history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian scholar who studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin. His posts included Heidelberg University (1980–1994) and First Director of the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

Harald Hundius was a Buddhist studies and linguistics scholar who studied under Singkha Wannasai (c. 1971–1974). He held posts as a lecturer at Chiang Mai University (1983) and professor at the University of Passau (c. 1993–2004).

Haraprasad Shastri was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar educated at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University. He served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1900–1908) and professor at the University of Dhaka (1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indology scholar who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948) and Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Ramakant Tripathi, and under doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

Haridas Bhattacharyya was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Scottish Church College (1915), the University of Calcutta (1917), and the University of Dhaka (1921).
Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi is an Indology scholar who studied under Karunapati Tripathi (attested 1996) and served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Muni Jinvijaya. He held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965), Gujarat University (1965–1975), and the L.D. Institute of Indology (c. 1975–2001).
